batches.title: Hard-Boil Eggs for Weekday Breakfasts (Mon–Fri)
steps: 1. Place 14 large eggs in a single layer in a large saucepan. Cover with cold water by 3 cm.
2. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce to medium and cook exactly 10 minutes.
3. Transfer eggs immediately to a bowl of ice-cold water. Leave 10 minutes to stop cooking.
4. Peel all eggs carefully. Pat dry with paper towel.
5. Place peeled eggs in a sealed airtight container lined with damp paper towel. Label 'Boiled Eggs — eat by Thursday'. Refrigerate.
yields: 14 peeled hard-boiled eggs (for 2 people × 2 eggs × 4 days: Tue–Fri)

day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Breakfast — Kefir & Banana Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough with Avocado: retrieve 2 eggs per person, halve and place on avocado-spread toast.
day_of_assembly.Wednesday: Breakfast — Kefir & Blueberry Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough with Feta: retrieve 2 eggs per person, halve and layer on toast with crumbled feta.
day_of_assembly.Thursday: Breakfast — Kefir & Strawberry Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough with Avocado: retrieve 2 eggs per person, halve and lay on avocado-topped sourdough with orange on side.
day_of_assembly.Friday: ⚠ Cook fresh today — do NOT use the Sunday batch (eggs cooked is only safe ~4 day(s); this is day 5).

storage.safety_note: Hard-boiled eggs: 1 week in shell, 5 days peeled in water. Scrambled/cooked dishes: 3–4 days.

batches.title: Cook Quinoa for Mon–Tue Lunches
steps: 1. Rinse 300 g dry quinoa in a fine mesh sieve under cold running water for 60 seconds to remove bitterness.
2. Add to a medium saucepan with 600 ml cold salted water (1 tsp salt).
3. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low. Cover and simmer 12 minutes.
4. Remove from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
5. Spread on a baking tray to cool to room temperature (about 15 min). Do not cover while hot.
6. Once cool, divide into two labelled containers: 'Quinoa — Mon Lunch' (Diego 120 g + Diana 90 g) and 'Quinoa — Tue Lunch' (Diego 120 g + Diana 90 g). Refrigerate.
yields: ~780 g cooked quinoa (from 300 g dry), portioned for 2 lunches

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl with Roasted Eggplant & Quinoa: reheat Diego's 120 g + Diana's 90 g quinoa in microwave 90 sec, use as bowl base.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Lunch — Asian Tilapia Bowl with Stir-Fried Broccoli, Bell Pepper & Quinoa: reheat Diego's 120 g + Diana's 90 g quinoa in microwave 90 sec, layer under stir-fried veg and tilapia.

storage.safety_note: Add a splash of water before reheating to restore moisture. Use within 3 days.

batches.title: Braise Spiced Beef for Mon & Tue Lunches/Dinners
steps: 1. Weigh out total beef: 720 g lean beef strips (for Monday lunch and Tuesday dinner) — or use two batches if needed. Cut into 3 cm pieces or strips.
2. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy pan or Dutch oven over high heat.
3. Brown beef in batches (do not crowd), 2 min per side. Set aside.
4. In same pan, add 3 tbsp tomato paste, 2 cloves minced garlic (or 1 tsp garlic powder), 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp dried oregano, and 200 ml water or stock.
5. Stir well, scraping up any browned bits. Return beef to pan.
6. Simmer on low heat, covered, 15 minutes until beef is tender and sauce is thick.
7. Portion into two labelled containers: 'Beef Stew — Mon Lunch' (Diego 150 g + Diana 110 g) and 'Beef Tacos — Tue Dinner' (Diego 150 g + Diana 110 g).
8. Cool completely before sealing. Refrigerate immediately. Use by Wednesday (day 3 limit).
yields: ~520 g cooked braised beef in sauce, portioned for Monday lunch and Tuesday dinner

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl with Roasted Eggplant & Quinoa: reheat Diego's 150 g + Diana's 110 g beef in a pan with a splash of water 3 min, serve over quinoa with lentils and eggplant.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Dinner — Mexican Beef & Black Bean Tacos with Roasted Bell Peppers & Corn Tortillas: reheat Diego's 150 g + Diana's 110 g beef in a pan with 2 tbsp water 3 min, mix in warm black beans and fill tortillas with roasted peppers.

storage.safety_note: Store in coldest part of fridge. Reheat to 74 °C before serving.

batches.title: Roast Mixed Vegetables (Eggplant, Zucchini, Broccoli, Bell Peppers) for Mon–Tue
steps: 1. Preheat oven to 200°C. Line two large baking trays with baking paper.
2. Tray A — Eggplant: Cube 400 g eggplant into 2 cm pieces. Toss with 1.5 tsp olive oil, 1 tsp cumin, 0.5 tsp paprika, salt and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
3. Tray B — Broccoli & Bell Pepper: Break 250 g broccoli into florets. Slice 250 g bell peppers. Toss together with 1.5 tsp olive oil, 0.5 tsp garlic powder, salt. Spread in a single layer.
4. Roast both trays at 200°C for 20–22 minutes, flipping halfway. Vegetables should be golden and slightly caramelised.
5. Cool on trays for 15 min. Transfer to labelled containers: 'Eggplant — Mon Lunch', 'Broccoli/Pepper — Tue Lunch', 'Peppers — Tue Dinner'. Refrigerate. Use within 4 days.

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl with Roasted Eggplant & Quinoa: reheat Diego's 100 g + Diana's 80 g roasted eggplant in microwave 60 sec, scatter over bowl.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Dinner — Mexican Beef & Black Bean Tacos: reheat Diego's 80 g + Diana's 80 g roasted bell pepper in microwave 60 sec, pile into tacos over beef-bean mix.

storage.safety_note: Cooked vegetables store well. Roasted veg can be eaten cold in salads.
